basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 26.' and it opens '(Vers. 26.) Et vocavit nomen ejus Enos: hic speravit invocare nomen Domini Dei. Quomodo'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 26.) Et vocavit nomen ejus Enos: hic speravit invocare nomen Domini Dei. Quomodo ADAM (אדם) homo interpretatur: ita et ENOS (אנוש) juxta Hebraeae linguae varietatem, homo vel vir dicitur. Et pulchre, quia hoc vocabulum habuit, de eo scriptum est, Tunc initium fuit invocandi nomen Domini: licet plerique Hebraeorum aliud arbitrentur, quod tunc primum in nomine Domini et in similitudine ejus fabricata [Al. fabricati] sint idola.
